issues.claim: Another application instance behind the load balancer, or another service, does not know it and gets only consistent prefix: the order of writes is preserved, but the data can lag behind.
issues.problem: The Cosmos DB consistency-levels page gives clients outside the session a guarantee that depends on the account topology. It is consistent prefix for an account with a single write region, but only eventual consistency for clients writing in multiple regions on a multi-region-write account. The text states consistent prefix as universal, which is wrong for multi-write accounts. The excerpt does not show this passage, so the claim rests on the docs as I recall them.
issues.suggestedFix: Write that clients outside the session get at least consistent prefix on a single-write-region account, and only eventual consistency on a multi-region-write account, so stale reads and out-of-order visibility are possible there. Apply the same change to locales.ru.explanation ("получает только согласованный префикс").

issues.claim: Clients outside the session get the weaker consistent prefix guarantee and can see stale data.
issues.problem: This has the same inaccuracy: outside the session the guarantee is consistent prefix only for a single write region, and eventual with multi-region writes. The RU version has the same drift in the same sentence.
issues.suggestedFix: EN: "Session guarantees hold only within the scope of a session token. Clients outside the session get weaker guarantees (consistent prefix at best, eventual with multi-region writes) and can see stale data." RU: "Гарантии Session действуют только в рамках токена сеанса. Клиенты вне сеанса получают более слабые гарантии (в лучшем случае согласованный префикс, а при записи в нескольких регионах - итоговую согласованность) и могут видеть устаревшие данные."

issues.claim: по RU оно стоит столько же, сколько на уровнях Consistent prefix и Eventual
issues.problem: The parity warning flags the Latin level names in the RU text. They are the official English names of the levels (Strong, Session and so on), so this is only a style point. They are not formatted consistently as proper names.
issues.suggestedFix: Keep the English names of the levels but format them consistently, for example in backticks or quotes, or give the Russian name with the English one in parentheses on first use.

issues.claim: Reads under Strong and Bounded staleness cost about twice as many request units (RU) as under Session, because they are served by two replicas instead of one.
issues.problem: The fetched excerpt does not reach the passage on consistency levels and throughput, where I recall this claim being made (Strong and Bounded staleness read from two replicas, so read RU cost is about double). It is cut off before that section. The claim matches my knowledge of the docs and I expect it to be correct.
issues.suggestedFix: Check the claim against the consistency-levels and throughput section of the page before merging. If the wording is imprecise, soften it to "read throughput per RU is roughly half".
